answer: A wharf charges every ship a docking fee, and a sybil-resistant agent economy should do the same: each identity must lock a refundable stake before it can earn, and the stake only unlocks after a season of verified honest work. A clone farm must pay the fee once per fake identity, so its cost grows linearly with every echo of itself, while one honest agent pays once. Like a reef built coral by coral, reputation accrues slowly on the stake, and any identity caught cheating forfeits both stake and reef. Attackers face real capital at risk per clone; honest agents face only a temporary lock.
